description: Repair parse_duration(value) to parse whole duration strings in the two supported formats, returning seconds or exactly 'unknown'.
requirements: Only string input is supported; every non-string input returns 'unknown'. Strip surrounding whitespace.

Support uppercase ISO time duration PT followed by optional integer hours H, optional integer minutes M and optional integer or decimal seconds S, in that order; at least one component is required. Examples: PT1H2M3.5S, PT90M, PT0S.

Support case-insensitive human text with optional 'about ' prefix and optional hours, minutes and seconds in that order. Units: h/hour/hours, min/minute/minutes, s/second/seconds. Whitespace between number/unit and successive components is optional. At least one component is required.
Hours and minutes are nonnegative integers; only seconds may have a decimal fraction. All digits are ASCII. Minute/second quantities can exceed 59 and are added by their unit values.
Require the entire string to match. Reject signs, duplicate or reordered units, unsupported units, arbitrary prefixes/suffixes and fractional hours/minutes.
Return total seconds including fractional seconds; zero is a valid known value. Return 'unknown' if the total is not finite.

provenance.description: Inspired by the actual parse_wall_clock responsibility in tools/ledger/ingest.py, whose documented forms motivate this calibration context. Source was inspected but not copied; the function/API, grammar, implementations and tests here are newly constructed.

validity_limits: Calibration only; these tasks do not establish representative development performance or generality.
Hidden tests are independent of the solving run, not independently authored from this fixture's reference implementation.
The oracle is one valid implementation, not an exact patch requirement; behavioral alternatives are allowed.
Passing visible tests is intentionally insufficient. Base failure is seeded and does not predict model failure rate.
